html:
Blender creative automation — October 13, 2026

Server source 0.3.6, Blender adapter 0.2.33. This increment adds nine MCP tools and retains existing inspection, scene recipe, rig, skin, UV and transfer tools. The source stdio registry contains 104 tools across both applications.

Discovery and execution are separate

blender_list_commands searches every registered bpy.ops identifier in the selected session. blender_inspect_command returns native RNA parameter schemas, ranges, enums, descriptions and the current context poll result. Catalog entries report create_object, mesh_operator, or discovery_only explicitly. A successful poll is not authorization, nor evidence that an execution adapter exists.

The Blender 5.2.2 factory-profile audit contains 2,499 operators, including 21 primitive creation operators and 44 registered audited mesh operators with execution adapters. The isolated source adapter registers five additional panel operators, yielding 2,504 discoverable operators. Installed add-ons can change these counts. The factory profile also exposes 4,012 RNA types.

  • blender_list_rna_types searches registered RNA types, including shader nodes, cameras, lights, modifiers, constraints, scenes and render settings.
  • blender_inspect_rna_type returns native type properties.
  • blender_inspect_properties returns values and per-property bridge editability for an explicit existing target. Use socket identifiers where names repeat.

Read the exported operator coverage [not indexed] or JSON catalog [not indexed]. These files report factory-profile coverage rather than pretending every discovered command executes.

Reviewed creative operations

Call blender_preview_creative with one request and an exact session_id, review the returned change, and call blender_apply_creative with both preview_id and confirmation equal to that reviewed ID. Previews expire after 600 seconds, are single-use, and reject changes to the captured scene content. Never replay an apply timeout: inspect the target and retained outputs first.

Supported request actions:

Action Behavior
create_object Native mesh, curve and NURBS primitives; cameras; Point, Sun, Spot and Area lights; Empty objects; worlds. Exact new names, bounded native parameters. make_active activates a new camera/world.
edit_properties Native numeric, boolean and enum properties on supported scene/render/image/color-management/Cycles/Eevee, object/data, node/socket, modifier and constraint targets. Pointer/collection/path and unrestricted attribute traversal are excluded.
create_material_graph A new material with up to 128 built-in shader nodes, 256 links, native settings and socket defaults, explicit color ramps, and optional assignment to a local mesh. Includes Blackbody, Emission, Voronoi, Noise, Vector Rotate, Layer Weight and Map Range rather than the old small node list.
keyframe Explicit native numeric keys for objects, cameras/lights, settings or shader sockets. Copies an existing Action, preserves the original datablock, and reevaluates the current frame.
mesh_operator An audited native mesh edit in Edit Mode on a copied plain mesh, selecting the full mesh. The original mesh datablock is retained; user context is restored. Shape keys, linked data and unsupported parameter types are rejected.
create_modifier Native non-simulation modifiers with numeric/enum settings. Existing modifier properties can be edited through edit_properties.
create_constraint Native object constraints with numeric/enum settings and optional exact assign_to target binding. Existing constraint properties can be inspected/edited.
save_copy Saves a new absolute .blend in an existing non-link directory, verifies file header/size/hash and preserves the active file path. Existing destinations are rejected. Reopening is separate validation.
render Saves a snapshot and launches a separate native Blender worker; produces a private PNG frame sequence without changing the interactive file, frame or render output path.

Property edits apply to the exact resolved datablock, including its other users if it is shared. Creation/mesh/keyframe workflows protect their original data as described above. All creative edits require Object Mode and run on Blender's main thread. Failures restore touched values and remove created data; rollback failure is reported explicitly. None of these operations imports anything into Unreal.

Example: native high-resolution sphere

{
  "action": "create_object",
  "name": "Sun_Photosphere",
  "type": "mesh.primitive_uv_sphere_add",
  "parameters": {"segments": 128, "ring_count": 64, "radius": 1.0}
}

Create an active camera with type: "CAMERA", make_active: true and object properties such as location. Inspect its camera target before editing lens, projection, clipping or orthographic scale. Camera orientation uses native Euler rotation in radians; it does not assume a viewing direction from a target name.

Example: 4K render settings

{
  "action": "edit_properties",
  "target": {"kind": "render"},
  "properties": {
    "engine": "CYCLES",
    "resolution_x": 4096,
    "resolution_y": 2304,
    "resolution_percentage": 100,
    "fps": 24
  }
}

Set the image_settings target to PNG first. A render request supplies frame_start and frame_end. Rendering returns state: running and a job_id; it never reports the started process as completed rendering.

blender_render_job_status checks worker exit, expected frame count and PNG headers/dimensions. completed requires exit code zero and all expected outputs. Full PNG decoding, visual checks and artistic approval remain separate. The bridge stays responsive while rendering. blender_cancel_render_job requires confirmation equal to the inspected job ID, terminates only that worker, and keeps the snapshot, log and partial frames. Poll a cancelling job until terminal state.

Job output is retained in the private Blender session root under renders/<session_id>/<job_id>. At most two workers run concurrently; ranges are limited to 1,000 frames and dimensions to 8,192 pixels per axis. External texture resources are not automatically packed. Job ownership lasts for the current adapter lifetime; adapter restart does not replay or resume uncertain work.

Remaining adapters

Discovery is broad; execution is deliberately described by tested workflow. Unrestricted Python/eval and arbitrary operator execution are not exposed. Scene loading/replacement, deletion, existing-file overwrite, preferences/add-on changes, file/network import operators, script nodes, Geometry Nodes/group and compositor graph authoring, simulations/cache baking, and specialized context-dependent editors still need dedicated reviewed adapters. Several existing rig/UV/transfer operations remain available through their original tools.

Verification and activation

  • Full Python suite: 330 passed.
  • Disposable native Blender 5.2.2 test: 39 checks passed, including wrong confirmation, replay, stale camera state, graph rollback, original mesh/Action preservation, native save-copy reopening and a real 4096 × 2304 render.
  • Real stdio MCP + disposable authenticated Blender: tool discovery, property schemas, sphere/camera/shader/key authoring, save-copy, two 4K animated frames, full PNG CRC/decompression checks, differing animated output, and cancellation.
  • Clean ZIP installation/activation/removal, cached-module reload and existing transfer/native tests passed in an isolated profile.

Evidence lives in Saved/creative-acceptance.json, Saved/creative-mcp-acceptance.json and Saved/BlenderPackageAcceptance-*. These tests do not establish interactive viewport QA or universal Blender control.

Installer: scripts/Install-ForgeBlender.ps1; package: Artifacts/ForgeMCP-Blender-Addon-0.2.33.zip. The installer preserves previous module bytes with timestamped backups and does not edit preferences or reload the running Blender process. Save any scene work before restarting Blender or toggling the add-on. Restart the ForgeMCP server/client connection to refresh the tool registry; verify server 0.3.6, adapter 0.2.33, and all nine new tools before continuing.
